text: A grant unto Thomas Sykes, of Sheffield, in the county of York, silversmith and gunsmith, of his new invented lock, instrument, or machine with one tricker or bolt, whereby both locks of a double barrel gun, pistol, blunderbuss, & all other fire arms of double barrels with two locks affixed thereto, are and may be fired, the one lock after the other, or one alone, by the said one tricker or bolt, without such side motion or alteration of the position of the said tricker or other inconvenience attending the same ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, & assigns, within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon- TAveed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inrol the same within one calendar month from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westminster, the 4th day of February, in the year of our Lord 1794. By writ, &c.
A grant unto Whitmore Baker, of Dedham, in the county of Essex, veterinary surgeon, for his invention of " An instrument or truss applicable to the nicking of horses tails"; 6 months.

A grant unto James Wood, of the parish of Saint Mary, Newington, in the county of Surrey, mathematical instrument maker, of his new invented machines for washing and wringing of linen, woollen, wool, cotton, silk, velvet, or any other commodity that requires washing, cleansing, or scouring ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, & asss, within Engd, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 yrs pursuant to the statute; with a clause to inrol the same within one calendar month from the date hereof. W. H. M. at West1', the 21st day of April, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Henry Crosley, of the firm of Henry Crosley, Son, and Galsworthy, of Emerson Street, in the county of Surrey, engineers and coppersmiths, for his invention of " Certain improved modes or methods of and apparatus for heating and lighting, for drying substances, and for employing air in a warm and cofd state for manufacturing purposes "; 6 months ; colonies.

A grant unto Peter Armand Le Comte he Fontainemoreau, of 15, New Broad Street, in the city of London, for " Certain improvements in the process and apparatus for treating fatty bodies and the matters producing them, such process and apparatus being equally applicable to the treating several other substances; and also for the process and apparatus necessary for the useful application of all those products being a communication ; 6 months.

A grant unto Charles Derosne, of Leicester Square, in the county of Middlesex, gentleman, in consequence of a communication made to him by 1829. a certain foreigner residing abroad, and invention by himself, is in possession of an invention for " Certain improvements in extracting sugar or syrups from cane juice and other substances containing sugar, and in refining sugar and syrups"; to hold, &c ; two months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto James Tarver, of Daventry, in the county of Northampton, iron founder, for his invention of " Certain improvements in machinery or apparatus for cutting, grinding, and dressing vegetable substances "; 6 months.

A grant unto George Cummings, of Ludgate Street, in the city of London, toyman, of his new invented composition to put on all sorts of skins, paper, or linnen for drawing or writing on with pen & ink or pencil, & rubbing clean of again, & other purposes therein menconed; to hold to him, his execrs, admrs, & assigns, within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon- Tweed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute; with a clause to inroll the same within 4 kalendar months from the date hereof. Witness His Matie at Westmr, the 31st day of March, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Dugald Clarke, of the parish of Sl Thomas-in-the-East, in the Island of Jamaica, esqre, of his new invented method of constructing and hanging the boiler and of applying the powers of the machine (commonly called a fire or steam engine) to the working of his new constructed sugar cane mill, and of all kinds of mills or engines whatsoever ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and town of Berwickupon-Tweed, and also in the colonies & plantations abroad, for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within 4 calendar months from the date thereof. W. H. M. at W., the 5th day of Janry, 1770. By writ, &c.

A grant unto James Freeman, of the parish of S1 Botolph, Bishopsgate, within the city of London, citizen and clockmaker, of his invention of a central second stop watch, vertical or horizontal, without the assistance of a compound motion ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, thro' England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed, and also in the colonies and plantations abroad, for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within 4 calendar months from the date thereof. W. H. M. at W., the 13th day of Decr, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Charles Chubb, of Saint Pauls Church Yard, in the city of London, patent lock manufacturer, for his invented "Certain improvements in the construction of latches, which may be used for fastening doors or gates"; to hold, &c ; six mos. By writ, &c

A grant unto Wit~tiAM Newron, of Chancery Lane, in the county of Middlesex, civil engineer, for “Improved machinery for cleaning wheat and other grain or seeds from smut and other injurious matters ”; being a communication ; six months.
A grant unto Henry Marriott, of Fleet Sl, in the city of London, ironmonger, for his invtd "Improvement on water closets"; to hold, &c; two mos. By writ, &c.
A grant unto Edward Clarence Siiepard, of Duke Street, in the city of Westminster, gentleman, for " Improvements in obtaining and applying motive power "; a communication ; 6 months.

A grant unto GEORGE SANDERSON, of the city of Exeter, watchmaker, of his new invented machine called a lunar & kalendar watch key ; to hold to him, his exec", adm", & assigns, within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed, and also in His Matie’s colonies & plantaéons abroad, for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within 4 kalendar months from the date hereof. Witness His Matie at Westm’, the 25th day of June, in the year above. sy writ, &¢.
A grant unto GEORGE Kemp, of Carnarvon, North Wales, doctor of medicine, for his invention of "A new method of obtaining motive power by means of electro-magnetism "; 6 months ; colonies.

A grant unto Joseph Moseley Elliot, of the parish of S* James, Clerkenwell, in the county of Middx, watchmaker, for his new or improved method of making and constructing repeaters or repeating watches and time pieces ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of W ales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date thereof. By writ, &c.
A grant unto John Watson, of Chorle}r, in the county of Lancaster, gentleman, for his invention of " Improvements in the construction of filters used in the manufacture of sugar"; 6 months.
A grant unto Daniel Wilson, of Earl Street, London, gentleman, for his invented " Certain improvements in the process of boiling and refining sugar "; to hold, &c ; six months to inroll. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Marc Isambard Brunel, of Lindsay Row, Chelsea, in the county of Middlesex, civil engineer, for his invtd " Method or methods for forming tunnels or drifts under ground "; to hold, &c ; six mos. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Joseph Sigmond, of Bath, in the county of Somerset, surgeon dentist, for his new invented preservative lotion and dentifrice, which he calls the British imperial lotion and dentifrice, for preserving and beautifying the teeth and gums; to hold him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and the town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date thereof. W. H. M. at Westm1', the 20th day of Nov1, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Joseph Slater, of Sharpies, near Bolton-in-the- Moors, in the county of Lancaster, bleacher, of hisn ew invented improvement in a machine for the finishing of bleached, dyed, and printed muslins ; to hold to him, his exors, adfhors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and the town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date thereof. W. H. M. at Westmr, the 4th day of July, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Jean Baptiste Paul Chappe, of Manchester, in the county of Lancaster, spinner and doubler, for his invention of " Certain improvements in machinery or apparatus for spinning and doubling cotton and other fibrous substances "; 6 months.

A grant unto John Haywood, of Long Acre, in the parish of Saint Martin-in-the-Fielcls, in the county of Mictx, draftsman and mechanic, of his new invented machine for working mills and engines without the aid of fire, water, or wind, or in aid of all or any of those or any other powers ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, & asss, within Engd, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed, and also within His Majesty's colonies and plantations abroad, for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inrol the same within one calendar month from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westr, the 8th day of May, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto William Symington, of Bromley, in the county of Middlesex, cooper, for his invention of " Certain improvements in the machinery for propelling vessels by steam, parts of which are also applicable to motive machinery of other descriptions, whether actuated by steam or by any other moving power"; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Uriah Lane the younger, of Lambsconduit Street, in the united parishes of Saint Andrew, Holborn, and Saint George-the-Martyr, in the county of Middlesex, straw hat manufacturer, for his invtd " An improvement in the platting of straw, and in manufacturing bonnets and other articles therefrom"; to hold, &c ; two months.

A grant unto John George Lacy, of Camomile Street, in the city of London, gun manufacturer, and Samson Davis, of East Smithfield, in the county of Middlesex, gun lock maker, for their invented " A certain improvement or improvements in the construction of guns and fire arms "; to hold, &c ; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto John Bootie, of the parish of Saint Martin-in-the- Fields, brazier, of his new invented method of tinning copper and brass vessels, that is to say, ship kettles and kitchen furniture, to prevent that pernicious poisonous matter called verdegrease from damaging provisions ; to hold to him, his executors, admors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within four calendar months from the date hereof. W. H. M. at W., the 13th day of August, in the year above. By writt, &c.

A grant unto Henry Johnson, of London, gent11, of his new invented water proof compound, and a vegetable liquid ; which liquid is for the purposes of bleaching, whitening, and cleansing woollens, linnens, cottons, and other articles, in a superior manner to any other method or preparation ; and also for preparing stuffs or cloths made of woollen, linnen, cotton, or silk, in order, o c 2 by the application of the afsd water proof compound, to render them impenetrable to wet, and more elastic and durable when made into garments ; to hold to him, his exors, adffiors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and the town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date thereof. W. H. M. at Westm1*, the 26th day of July, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Hugh Cogan, merchant and manufacturer, of West George Street, Glasgow, in the county of Lanark, for his invention of "An improved method or methods for weaving in patterns or various colours or fabrics "; 6 months.

A grant unto Grorce Puities, of Park Street, Islington, in the county of Middlesex, chemist, for his invention of “ Certain improvements in the purification of certain oils and spirits”; 6 months ; colonies.

A grant unto Bexner Woopcrort, of Manchester, in the county palatine of Lancaster, printer, for his invented or discovered ‘ Certain improvements in the construction and adaption of a revolving spiral paddle for propelling boats and other vessels on water”; to hold, &¢; six months. By writ, &.

A spiall priviledge graunted to David Ramsey, Michaell Arnold, and John Ayliffe, and their assignes, for the terme of xiiijen yeares next ensuinge, of the sole usinge and excisinge (wthin England and Wales) as well of a new invencon by them invented and pfected for the boyling of great or little brewing vessells of liquor or other vessells used by dyers, soapeboylers, saltmaker, saltpeter makers, and for the dryinge of bricks and all manner of tyles wth seacoales, as of an invencon for the making and dryinge of pan tyles, stone juggs, bottles, melting potts for gouldsmithes, and other earthen comodities also with seacoles, wch nowe are made in forraine pts — paying yearely to the Crowne a fourthe pte of the profitt of the said invcncons. And they are to give an iust accompt yearely upon oath before one of the barons of the excheq1', and shall pay the said fourth pt into the receipt of excheq1'; with the ordinary proviso that if this graunt shall be found to be contry to lawe or inconvenient the same to be void. Teste apud Westm1", xvij° Feb, anno pd. p bre &c.

A grant unto William Keates, of Liverpool, in the county of Lancaster, merchant, for his invention of " Improvements in machinery for manufacturing rollers and cylinders used for calico printing and other purposes "; 6 months.

A grant unto Samuel Shorthouse, of Dudley, in the coy of Gloucester, for his invented " Machine to cut straw of any length required, thereby rendering straw a better and more convenient winter food for cattle, and the manure produced in farm yards, &c, fit for immediate use ; also for rendering dry straw a manageable manure ; also for cutting straw to mix with horses corn ; also for cutting straw to any given length for any other purpose"; to hold, &c ; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto ALEXANDER ViviAN, of Gwennap, near Redruth, in | the county of Cornwall, gent", for his invention of “ An improved apparatus for dressing ores”; 6 months. | 9965. A grant unto Joserm Rock jun. of Birmingham, factor, for his

A grant unto John Manton, of Dover Street, in the parish of S* George, Hanover Square, in the county of Middlesex, gunmaker, of his new invention or improvement in the construction of guns and pistols of every description ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and the town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inrol the same within one calendar month from the date thereof. W. H. M. at Westr, the 12th day of April, in the year above. By writ, &c.
A grant unto William GoSSAGE, of Neath, metallurgist, for his invention of " Improvements in obtaining products from certain ores and other compounds of certain metals'*: 6 months.
A grant unto Louis Francois Feuillet, of Paris, but now of George Yard, Lombard Street, in the city of London, gentleman, for his invention of "Improvements in casting type for printing"; 6 months.

A grant unto Ricuarp Ress, of Red Lion Passage, in the county of Middx, cutler, for his invented certain improvements in trusses for persons afflicted with ruptures ; to hold to him, his exors, adMors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date thereof. By writ, &

A grant unto Richard Fish wick, of Elswick, in the parish of Newcastle-upon-Tyne, in the county of Northumberland, of his new method of making white lead ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, & asss, within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar | month from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westminster, the 15th day of January, in the year above. Bv writ, &c.

A grant unto Richard Trevithick, of Rotherhithe, in the county of Surrey, engineer, and Robert Dickinson, of Great Queen Street, in the county of Middx, esq1", for their invented new method or way of stowing cargoes of ships and other vessels, by means of packages for containing goods and products of certain descriptions destined for conveyances by sea not hitherto employ'd, by which means expences of stowage room will be saved, and the contents be rendered more safe against damage ; to hold to them, their exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed, and in all our colonies and plantations abroad, for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within six calendar months from the date thereof; and also with a clause for supplying His Majesty's service with all such articles of the said invention as shall be required by the commrs of the navy and the elder brethren of the Trinity House for the time being. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Enoch Steel and William Britter, both of Lambeth, in the county of Surrey, manufacturers, for their invention of " Improi ements in the manufacture of tobacco pipes"; 6 months ; colonies.

A grant unto Mathew Elliston and Tho. Winter of the sole vse, exercise, and benefitt of their new invencon, being a new sort of mills moved with jackworks and wheeles as by the strength of men only, without the help either of wind or water, to grind corne and move saws, very vsefull where other mills are not, as in the West Indies ; to hold and enjoy the same for 14 yeares according to the statute ; with usuall clauses. Testib apud Westm, 9° Octob, anno supradco. By writt, &c.

A grant unto John McCurdy, of Great James Street, Bedford Row, in the coy of Middx, gent., that a communication has been made to him by a foreigner residing abroad by which he is in possession of an invention or discovery of " Certain improvements in the method of constructing mills and mill stones for grinding"; to hold, &c ; two months. By writ, &c.
A grant unto Henry Mandeville Meade, of the city of New York, in the United States of America, gentleman, for " Improvements in the manufacture of bread"; being a communication ; 6 months.

A grant unto Jame s Storey, of the Loav Lights, in the parish of Tynemouth, in the county of Northumberland, esquire, of his new invented machine for drawing of coals, lead, tin, and other materials out of mines ; to administrators, and assigns, within England, hold to him, his executors, -upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years Wales, and town of Berwick a clause to inroll the same within one calendar pursuant to the statute ; with W. H. M. at Westminster, the fourth day of month from the date hereof. By writt, &c. February, in the year above.

A grant unto Abraham Foster, of Seething Lane, in the parish of Allhallows, Barking, peruke maker, of his new invented composicon for curing the ague, called Foster's composicon; to hold to him, his execrs, admrs, & assigns, within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within 4 kalendar months from the date hereof. Witness His Matie at Westm1', the 15th day of April, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto George Beadon, of Taunton, in the county of Somerset, commander in Her Majesty's navy, and Andrew Smith, of Princes Street, Leicester Square, in the county of Middlesex, engineer, for their invention of " Improvements in warping or hauling vessels ; which improvements are also applicable to moving other bodies"; 6 months ; colonies.

A grant unto Thomas Wade, of Nelson Place, Kent Road, in the parish of Sl George, Southwark, in the county of Surrey, gent", for his invented method or process of imitating lapis lazuli, porphry, jasper, the various sorts of kinds of marble, and all other stones usually wrought, carved, sculptured, or polished ; also inlaid or mosaic work, to be used for or in the formation of manufacture of chimney pieces, slabs, funeral monuments, and for every other purpose to which such stones and marbles are or may be applied ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain & Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed, and also in all our colonies and plantations abroad, for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within two calendar months from the date thereof. By writ, &c.
A grant unto Thomas Moorcroft Benbow, of Birmingham, surgeon, for " Improvements in fastenings for surgical and other bandages, and for articles of dress "; 6 months.
A grant unto Moses Poole, of the Patenl Office, London, gentleman, for " Improvements in combining caoutchouc with other matters"; 6 months ; a communication.

A grant unto William Mollt, of Bedford Square, in the county of Middx, for his invented improved method of acting upon machinery ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within six calendar months from the date thereof. By writ, &c.

A grant unto John Williams, of Cornhill, in the city of London, stationer, for his invented " Method to prevent the frequent removal of the pavement and carriage paths for laying down & taking up pipes, and for other purposes, in streets, roads, & public ways"; to hold, &c; two months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Thomas Lightfoot, of Jarrow Paper Mills, South Shields, in the county of Durham, paper manufacturer, for his invention of "Improvements in machinery applicable to the manufacture of paper "; 6 months.

A grant unto Thomas Barber Bryant, of Great Yarmouth, in the county of Norfolk, and of Dunbar, in the county of East Lothian, in Scotland, sail cloth and rope maker, of his new invention of improving the oil of whales; to hold to him, his executors, administrators, and assigns, within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westminster, the twentieth day of December, in the year above. By writ.

A grant unto William Losh, of the town and county of Newcastleupon-Tyne, iron founder, and George Stephenson, of Killingworth, in the coy of Northumberland, engineer, for their invtd "New method or new methods of facilitating the conveyance of carriages, and all manner of goods and materials along rail ways and frame ways, by certain inventions and improvements in the construction of the machine, carriages, carriage wheels, rail ways, & frame Avays employed for that purpose "; to hold, &c; 2 mos.
A grant unto James Hancock, of Sidney Square, Mile End, in the county of Middlesex, civil engineer, for his invention of " An improved method of raising water and other fluids "; 6 months.
A grant unto Henrik Zander, of North Street, Sloane Street, in the county of Middlesex, gentleman, for his invention of " Improvements in the manufacture of paper "; 6 months.

A grant unto John Duff, of Great Pulteney Street, in the coy of Middx, cutler, that in consequence of a communication made to him by a foreigner he is in possession of an invention of snuffers, on a new and improved construction ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain & Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date thereof. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Henry Raminger, of the parish of Christ Church, in the county of Surry, of his new invented engines or machines, whereby shots comonly used for fowling & bullets of lead are made more exactly round, solid, and to much greater perfection than hath been hitherto practiced ; to hold to him, his execrs, admrs, & assigns, within England, Wales, & town of Berwickupon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within three kalendar months from the date hereof. Witness His Matie at Westm1, the 29th day of June, in the year above. By writ, &c.
A grant unto Joseph Burch, county of Surrey, calico printer, for his invention of " Certain improvements in printing cotton, woollen, paper, and other fabrics and materials "; 6 months.

A grant unto Thomas Williams, of Broad Street, in the parish of Sl James, within the liberty of Westm1, in the county of Middx, apothecary, of his new invented medicine, called essence of flowers of benzion or pulmonic drops; to hold to him, his execrs, admrs, & assigns, within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed, and His Matie's plantacons & colonies abroad, for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute; with a clause to inroll the same within four kalendar months from the date hereof. Witness His Matie, as next above. By writ, &c.
A grant unto John Nott, of the city of Cork, gentleman, for his invention of "Certain improvements in the means of communicating intelligence from one place to another"; 6 months.

A grant unto Joseph Collett, of the parish of Saint Clements Danes, in the county of Middx, dealer in medicine, of his new invencon of an elixir which is an effectual cure for the dropsy and jaundice, and affords immediate relief, if not an effectual cure, for the stone & gravel; to hold to him, his excrs, admrs, & assigns, within England, Wales. & town of Berwick-upon- Tweed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute in that behalf ; and a clause is inserted obliging him particularly to describe the nature of his said invencon, by an instrument in writing under his hand & seal, to be inrolled in the High Court of Chancery within four kalendar months from the date hereof. Witness His Matie at Westmr, the 17th day of Febry, in the year above. By writt, &c.

A grant unto Joun VENABLEs, of Burslem, in the county of Stafford, earthenware manufacturer, and JonHn Tunniciirr, of Burslem aforesaid, bricklayer, for their invention of “ A new and improved method of building and constructing ovens used by potters and china manufacturers in the firing of their wares”; 2 months.

A grant unto Alpiionse Rene Le Mire de Normandy, of Red Cross Square, in the parish of Cripplegate, in the city of London, doctor of medicine, for his invention of " Certain improvements in the manufacture of soap "; 6 months.
A grant unto William Willcocks Sleigh, physician and surgeon, of London, for his invention of " A counteracting reaction motive-power engine"; 6 months ; colonies.

A grant unto James Knowles junior, of Bolton-lc-Moors, in the county of Lancaster, coal merchant, and Alonzo Buonaparte Woodcock, of Manchoster, in the said county, engineer, for their invention of " Certain improvements in machinery or apparatus to be employed for raising coal or other matters from mines ; which improvements are also applicable to raising or lowering men or animals, or other similar purposes"; 6 months.
A grant unto Ernst Kaemmerer, of Bromberg, in the kingdom of Prussia, ironfounder, for his invention of "Improvements in sowing, depositing, or distributing seeds over land"; 6 months ; colonics.

A grant unto Frederick Koenig, of Castle Street, Finsbury Square, printer, for his invented further improvements on his method of printing by means of machinery ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Gl Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; witli a clause to inroll the same within six calendar months from the date thereof. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Matthew Cotes Wyatt, of Henrietta Street, Cavendish Square, in the parish of Saint Mary-le-bone and county of Middx, esquire, in consequence of a communication made to him by a certain foreigner residing abroad he is possessed of " A safeguard to prevent the accidental movement of the cock of a gun, pistol, or other fire arm forward towards the hammer ;" that the same are new in this kingdom, &c ; to hold, &c ; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto James Slater, of Salford, in the county of Lancaster, gentleman, for his invention of "Certain improvements in steam engines, and also in boilers and in furnaces used for the generation of steam, or other useful purposes"; 6 months.

A grant unto Richard Burgess, of Northwick, in the county of Chester, M.D., for his invented " A drink for the cure, prevention, or relief of gout, gravel, and other diseases, which may be also applied to other uses "; to hold, &c ; two months. By writ, &c.
A grant unto Joun Davis, of Brettel Lane, in the county of Stafford, glass manufacturer, for his invention of “A certain improvement or certain improvements in or applicable to lamps”; 6 months.

A grant unto Thomas Crook, of Great Queen Street, Lincoln's Inn Fields, in the county of Middlesex, coachmaker, and Thomas German, of Baldwin's Gardens, in the said county of Middlesex, gentleman, of their new invented machine, contrivance, or device, for the prevention and cure of smoaking chimnies; to hold to them, their exors, admors, & asss, within Engd, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 yrs pursuant to the statute; with a clause to inrol the same within one calendar month from the date hereof. W. H. M. at West1", the 12th day of Jahry, in the year above. By writ, &c.
A grant unto John Barsham, of Chelmsford, in the county of Essex, manufacturer, for his invention of " Improvements in separating the fibre from cocoa-nut husks"; 6 months.

A grant unto William Row, of Newcastle-upon-Tyne, merch1, for his new invented mineral lamp black ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed, and also in all the colonies and plantations abroad, for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date thereof. W. H. M. at Westm1, the 14th day of July, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Robert Goodacre, of Ullesthorpe, near Lutterworth, in the county of Leicester, for his invention of " An apparatus for raising heavy loads in carts or other receptacles containing the said loads when it is required that the unloading should take place at any considerable elevation above the ground"; 6 months.
A grant unto Josias Christopher Gamble, of Saint Helens, in the county of Lancaster, manufacturing chemist, for " Improvements in the manufacture of sulphuric acid"; 6 months.

A grant unto George Henry Bursill, of River Lane, Lower Road, Islington, in the county of Middlesex, gentleman, for his invention of "An improved method or methods of weighing, and certain improvements in weighing machines"; 6 months.
